root_causes.description: The shipping service exhibits a severe latency anomaly (p99 up to 9622ms, max 9650ms, mean ~5700ms) sustained across the entire incident window. The fault is intrinsic to shipping: error rate is near zero (max 0.012), CPU is flat at 0.002 cores, memory is flat at ~12.5MB, pod restarts are 0, and its only downstream dependency (quote) is healthy at 1.98ms p99. This is consistent with an injected processing delay inside the shipping service rather than resource pressure, crashes, errors, or dependency failure.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms < 100ms for shipping (its dependency quote responds in ~2ms)

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.004, p50=0.000, p95=0.011, p99=0.012, max=0.012 — no error spike
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; confirms latency-only fault, not http_abort

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage flat at 0.002 cores (mean=p50=p95=p99=max=0.002) across window
evidence.expected_baseline: no cpu_stress; rules out CPU saturation as cause
no memory_stress; rules out memory pressure

root_causes.description: Hypothesis that shipping latency was caused by its downstream dependency quote (shipping → quote per topology) failing or slowing down. Investigated and ruled out: quote's p99 latency is a flat 1.98ms across the entire window, so the delay does not originate from the quote dependency.

evidence.expected_baseline: quote healthy; downstream dependency failure ruled out as root cause

root_causes.description: Hypothesis that shipping was failing requests (error/abort fault) causing upstream slowness. Ruled out: error rate stays near zero (max 0.012), no error traces found for shipping in the window, and no error logs found for shipping in the window.

evidence.observed_value: [no traces found] — no shipping traces (including error traces) returned in window
evidence.expected_baseline: error traces present if http_abort fault active; absence supports latency-only fault

evidence.observed_value: [no logs found] — no error logs for shipping in window
evidence.expected_baseline: error logs present if http_abort fault active; absence supports latency-only fault

remediation_steps: Inspect the shipping service deployment for recently introduced artificial delays (e.g., latency fault flags in flagd feature-flag config, sleep() calls in shipping handlers, or a bad image rollout) and roll back the offending change.
Check flagd feature-flag evaluation for shipping-related latency flags and disable any experimental delay flags.
Add a p99 latency SLO alert on shipping (e.g., p99 > 500ms for 2m) so latency-only faults are detected even when error rate stays at zero.
Review impact on checkout and frontend, since checkout→shipping and frontend→shipping call paths absorb the ~5-9.6s delay and degrade user-facing checkout performance.
After remediation, confirm shipping p99 returns to sub-100ms baseline and quote dependency remains healthy.
